cases.text: Tech Lead Backend Engineer. Lead a small Node.js team and design APIs in TypeScript and PostgreSQL.
cases.rationale: Lead changes seniority; backend remains the browseable discipline.

cases.text: Senior Frontend Engineer. Work with React, TypeScript and accessibility. Mentor teammates occasionally.
cases.rationale: Occasional mentoring alone must not promote a senior IC vacancy to LEAD.

cases.text: Principal Data Architect. Own the data platform architecture, Kafka pipelines and warehouse strategy.
cases.rationale: The discipline is data engineering; explicit Principal supports the level.

cases.text: Security Architect. Define cloud security controls and threat modelling for AWS services.
cases.rationale: Architect preserves the security discipline, but the title alone does not establish principal-level scope.

cases.text: CTO for a SaaS startup. Set engineering strategy, hire leaders and remain accountable for platform architecture.
cases.rationale: Executive technical leadership is not silently mapped to a coding specialty.

cases.text: CTO for a marketing agency. Own vendor selection, office IT and business technology budgets.
cases.rationale: A senior title at a technology-using company is not automatically an in-scope engineering role.

cases.text: Software Engineer. Build internal services in Go; the posting gives no clearer product discipline.
cases.rationale: Generic Software Engineer is permitted only as an explicit escape hatch, not a fallback for a known discipline.

cases.text: Software Engineer, backend focus. Design REST APIs, PostgreSQL data models and asynchronous Go services.
cases.rationale: Specific backend evidence beats the generic title.

cases.text: Machine Learning Engineer. Productionize ranking models, feature pipelines and model monitoring.
cases.rationale: ML engineering is an approved distinct discipline.

cases.text: Data Analyst. Build BI dashboards, SQL reports and product metrics for stakeholders.
cases.rationale: Analytics is not silently folded into Data Engineer.

cases.text: Senior QA Automation Engineer. Create Playwright regression suites and CI quality gates.
cases.rationale: Automation QA is more specific than the QA parent role.

cases.text: Manual QA Engineer. Test web releases, write test cases and report defects; no automation responsibilities.
cases.rationale: Manual and automation QA must remain distinguishable.

cases.text: iOS Engineer. Ship native Swift and SwiftUI features for a consumer application.
cases.rationale: The mobile platform is known and should not collapse to a generic mobile role.

cases.text: Cross-platform Mobile Engineer. Build Android and iOS applications in Flutter.
cases.rationale: Cross-platform is distinct from an iOS-only or Android-only role.

cases.text: Product Manager. Define roadmaps, interview customers and coordinate design and engineering teams.
cases.rationale: Product management is out of the approved engineering-role scope.

cases.text: Platform Engineer. Operate Kubernetes, Terraform and CI/CD for internal developer infrastructure.
cases.rationale: The approved taxonomy treats platform engineering as the DevOps discipline.
